Specifically, this paper proposes a novel approach called *Adaptive Ensembling* (AE) which uses an ensemble of ensembles (EOE) and unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) techniques to discover pertinent sub-corpora without manual labeling. Our model first extracts document embeddings from a large corpus of documents in a target language, then it transfers the document embeddings learned in the source language into the target language. This process helps AE achieve an automatic selection of relevant sub-corpora. In order to evaluate our method, we use two real-world datasets: one contains US presidential speeches and the other contains US Supreme Court opinions. We compare our method against other baseline methods and the results show that our proposed method, Adaptive Ensembling, can effectively extract relevant documents even when the proportion of pertinence in the document corpus is less than 15%, which outperforms the baseline methods.

Abstract

A method is described for the identification of astaxanthin glucoside esters from snow alga *Chlamydomonas nivalis* by means of liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry with atmospheric pressure chemical ionization. The aim was to identify and characterize astaxanthin glucoside esters in this species of algae by using an LC-APCI-MS method. Chromatographic separation was achieved using a reversed phase column with a gradient of acetonitrile-water containing 0.1% formic acid as the mobile phase. Metabolites were identified based on their retention time and mass spectrometric information, which included accurate mass, fragment ions and adduct ions. We were able to successfully identify two different diglucoside diesters of astaxanthin and confirm their structure by using HRESI-MS and 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy. This work represents the first report of the isolation and characterization of astaxanthin glucoside esters from *C. nivalis*.

The Fe3O4 magnetic core is well dispersed in the poly(methoxy polyethylene glycol)-block-poly(butyl acrylate)-block-poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) shell, and the particles exhibited superparamagnetic property and temperature responsive swelling and shrinking behavior. Therefore, the microspheres prepared by this method could be used in many application areas such as drug delivery, biological separation and purification, biomedical imaging, and magnetic hyperthermia.

Abstract:
Leibowitz and his colleagues found that accommodation rests at an intermediate distance that shows wide interindividual variation. They proposed that this intermediate dark focus is useful for correcting anomalous refractive errors, but this proposal was later questioned when different measurement techniques yielded conflicting results. In the present study, we sought to develop a computational model to predict optimal accommodative performance from measures of the dark focus of accommodation. Our study included 21 young adults who were all full-time contact lens wearers with no history of eye disease or eye surgery. The dark focus of accommodation was measured using an aberrometer (Optovue RTA-200). We also performed subjective refraction testing and a cycloplegic refraction on each participant. The accommodative amplitude of these participants was also measured using a dynamic retinoscopy system (Reichert AccuRet). We trained a machine learning model to predict accommodative amplitude from dark focus measurements, and validated the model on a separate data set of 14 young adult contact lens wearers. We found that the proposed model was able to accurately predict accommodative amplitude from dark focus measures in both the training and validation data sets. These results suggest that the dark focus of accommodation could be a promising predictor of accommodative performance, which has implications for contact lens fitting and presbyopia correction.

Abstract

Currently, traditional family values that have been passed down through generations appear to be at risk. This has significant implications for the stability and health of individuals, families, and communities. This article explores selected issues related to intergenerational transmission of family values. In the introduction, we discuss the changing social environment that impacts family values and traditions and the need to understand this change in order to maintain healthy relationships and stable communities. The literature review covers the definition of family values, the concept of generational change, and the intergenerational transmission of family values. We discuss that some of the challenges in the modern world may contribute to the decline of family values, such as the change in social media and how it affects communication between generations. We further argue that intergenerational family traditions may also be an important part of family life, helping to keep the family together and pass down cultural knowledge from one generation to the other. The methodology is described briefly which included surveying 100 parents, 100 teenagers and 100 grandparents regarding their views on passing down family values through generations, including the importance of traditions, the reasons why they are not able to pass down traditions and what can be done to help preserve family traditions. Our findings show that most parents and grandparents think that they should be passing down family values and traditions to their children and grandchildren but the main reason they are not able to do so is due to their busy schedules. In the conclusion, we present our summary of the findings and suggest a number of recommendations to improve the transmission of family values and traditions, including having open communication within families, setting time aside to share stories or traditions and involving teenagers more in these activities.

generations.raw_text: Two critical points in the energetics of muscular contraction have been re-examined: (1) the absence of heat production after the active state has ended (i.e. in 'relaxation'), and (2) the mobilization of ATP during muscle contraction and its relation to the rate of tension development. The first critical point challenges a long-held belief that no heat is produced in the relaxation phase of a muscle. We found evidence that heat is indeed produced at this time. The second point was to investigate if there is a direct relationship between the rate of ATP mobilization and the rate of tension development during muscle contraction and if they could be used to predict each other. Our results indicated that ATP mobilization can predict the rate of tension development but not vice versa. We propose that ATP mobilization is more directly related to Ca2+ mobilization, which controls the rate of tension development. Our findings suggest that the two critical points in the energetics of muscular contraction need to be revised. This research will help researchers understand better the energetics of muscular contraction.

However, despite this standard treatment, recurrent stroke still occurs in a significant proportion of these patients. Objectives: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the risk of recurrent stroke in patients with ICAS treated with AMM compared to patients enrolled in the SAMMPRIS trial. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed a cohort of patients who were treated with AMM for ICAS at our institution from 2014 to 2019. The primary outcome measure was the rate of recurrent stroke in the first 2 years after initiation of AMM. We compared these results to the recurrence rates of stroke in the SAMMPRIS trial. The rate of recurrent stroke in the first 2 years after initiation of AMM was 8.7%. The SAMMPRIS trial had a rate of recurrent stroke of 4.7% over a median follow-up time of 54 months. Conclusion: Our study found that the rate of recurrent stroke in patients with ICAS treated with AMM was higher than the rate in the SAMMPRIS trial. Future work will focus on trying to identify risk factors for recurrent stroke in this patient population and to evaluate if other interventional or medical strategies may have better outcomes in this patient group.
